analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free is caused by delayed secure-channel cleanup freeing a channel_list_entry while stale pointers to that channel remain in manager/session state, leading to a second cleanup during server destruction. removeSecureChannel() schedules removeSecureChannelCallback(entry) via UA_Server_delayedCallback and detaches from the manager list, but does not robustly prevent later teardown paths from touching the same channel/session linkage; then UA_Server_run_shutdown processes delayed callbacks (freeing entry/channel), and UA_Server_delete -> UA_SecureChannelManager_deleteMembers/UA_SecureChannel_deleteMembersCleanup traverses channel->sessions and reads freed session headers.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In fuzz_binary_message, attacker-controlled binary messages create at least one session on a secure channel (CreateSession path), then trigger channel close/timeout/removal so removeSecureChannel() queues delayed free. During harness teardown, UA_Server_run_shutdown executes delayed callbacks first (freeing channel entry/session-related memory), and subsequent UA_Server_delete cleanup re-enters secure-channel/session cleanup on stale linkage, producing UAF. The PoV’s sequence of OPN/MSG/CLO chunks drives this state mismatch.
